samples.summary: Adoption fixes only the undo half of the `saveSnapshot(); withUndoUnit(...)` collision; the redo half still diverges between the two stores. `snapshot()` unconditionally does `this.redoStack = []` (memory.ts:183) *before* `batch()` runs, so when the body writes nothing, `batch()`'s `priorRedo` restore (memory.ts:253) puts back an already-emptied stack. On `YorkieDocStore` `snapshot()` is a no-op and an empty batch pushes no change, so `doc.history` keeps its redo entries. The delta's own new documentation asserts parity — text-editor.ts:3831-3836 ("That ordering costs nothing on `YorkieDocStore` ... and nothing on `MemDocStore` either") and docs-collaboration.md:342-353 ("That ordering has to cost nothing on either store"), plus memory.test.ts's existing "a batch that writes nothing leaves redo history intact" case which encodes the shared contract but does not exercise the snapshot-before-batch shape. Concretely: in a slides text box or the demo app, undo once (redo now available) then perform any editor action that opens a unit and writes nothing (e.g. Backspace at the start of the box, which still calls `saveSnapshot()` above `withUndoUnit`) and redo is silently dead, where the Yorkie-backed docs editor keeps it. The two stores give two answers to the one documented contract.

samples.summary: The adoption seam is an implicit structural-equality heuristic rather than an explicit contract, and as a side effect a top-level `batch()` can now delete an undo checkpoint it did not create. When `adopted` is true and the body writes nothing, the `wroteNothing` branch pops an entry that was pushed by an earlier, unrelated `snapshot()` call — pinned by the new test "snapshot() before a batch that writes nothing costs no undo unit", which asserts `canUndo() === false` on a stack the batch never contributed to. The store cannot distinguish "the caller's own pre-batch checkpoint" from "any older checkpoint that happens to hold an identical document", so the guarantee rests on a value comparison instead of a stated API (e.g. an explicit `batch(fn, { adoptPendingSnapshot: true })` or a store-level `snapshotFor(batch)` seam). It behaves as specified for the `saveSnapshot(); withUndoUnit(...)` shape, so the cost stays inside the codebase, but it makes `snapshot()` non-durable in a way `DocStore`'s doc comments (store.ts:54) do not describe.
samples.evidence: memory.ts:220-226 `const adopted = top !== undefined && JSON.stringify(top) === beforeJson; ... if (!adopted) this.undoStack.push(before);` with memory.ts:248-254 popping `before` on `wroteNothing`.

samples.summary: The `DocStore` interface documentation was not updated for the new batch/snapshot interaction. `store.ts` still describes `snapshot()` as "MemDocStore pushes a checkpoint" and `batch()` as taking its own, with no mention that a checkpoint taken immediately before a top-level batch is adopted (and may be discarded when the body writes nothing). The behavioural rule now lives only in `MemDocStore`'s implementation comment, `link-run.ts`'s function doc and `docs-collaboration.md`; the interface that both stores implement — the natural home for a two-store contract — is silent, so the next store implementation has no way to know the rule exists.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:54 comment describing snapshot()/batch() semantics, unchanged by this delta.

verdict.reason: All claimed evidence checks out verbatim. memory.ts:177-184 `snapshot()` unconditionally clears `this.redoStack` outside a batch; batch() reads `const priorRedo = this.redoStack` at memory.ts:225 — which, in the documented `saveSnapshot(); withUndoUnit(...)` ordering, is already the emptied stack — so the `this.redoStack = priorRedo` restore at memory.ts:253 restores nothing. YorkieDocStore diverges: snapshot() is an explicit no-op (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2951-2954), an empty batch pushes no Yorkie change (2909-2949), and canRedo() delegates to doc.history (2980-2982), so redo survives. Both the new code comment (text-editor.ts:3827-3837) and the design doc (docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:342-358) assert the ordering "has to cost nothing on either store", so the two implementations of the one DocStore contract give two answers. The existing test memory.test.ts:374-392 pins the empty-batch redo contract but snapshots before the write, not immediately before the batch, and the adoption test at 317-337 asserts only canUndo — so nothing covers this shape. Reachable: the snapshot-above-unit ordering is used at text-editor.ts:832-834, 1013-1019, 1550-1551, 2649-2651, 2673-2674, and no-write paths exist (handleBackspace 2499-2501, handleWordBackspace 2599-2612). No guard elsewhere restores the cleared redo stack, so no refutation ground applies; under this lens it is a divergence-between-duplicated-implementations with a user-visible cost.

finding.summary: `saveSnapshot()` before `withUndoUnit()` double-counts undo on MemDocStore, so every batched edit costs a dead Cmd+Z in slides text boxes and the docs demo app
finding.evidence: The new rule is "`saveSnapshot()` must be called before opening a unit, never inside one" (text-editor.ts:3807, docs-collaboration.md:335). On `MemDocStore` the undo unit is anchored to the checkpoint, not to an update: `snapshot()` pushes a clone (memory.ts:177-184) and then `batch()` pushes *another* pre-body clone up front (memory.ts:199-209), skipping the double-push only when `batchDepth > 0`. So `handleInput`/`handleEnter`/`applyPastePlan`/`pasteFromClipboard` now push two identical undo entries per action: the first Cmd+Z restores the pre-edit document, the second appears to do nothing and consumes a history slot. This is exactly the "first Cmd+Z looked like it did nothing" symptom `withNamedStyleChange` avoids by calling `docStore.snapshot()` *inside* `doc.batch()` (editor.ts:1238-1239). MemDocStore is not dev-only: slides text boxes run this same `TextEditor` with `MemDocStore` and wire `saveSnapshot = () => docStore.snapshot()` and `undoAction = () => docStore.undo()` (text-box-editor.ts:431, 680-683), so Slides in-textbox undo is affected in production. Nothing in the diff (contract text in store.ts, memory.ts, or the new tests, which all use `YorkieDocStore`) covers the Mem path.

verdict.reason: The finding's central mechanism does not exist in the code. It claims `MemDocStore.batch()` unconditionally pushes a second pre-body clone, skipping only when `batchDepth > 0`, so `saveSnapshot()` before `withUndoUnit()` double-counts. In fact memory.ts:220-226 compares the top of the undo stack by value against the current document and ADOPTS an identical existing checkpoint (`const adopted = top !== undefined && JSON.stringify(top) === beforeJson; ... if (!adopted) this.undoStack.push(before);`) — precisely the snapshot-then-batch ordering the finding says is unhandled. The comment at memory.ts:206-219 names this scenario and the exact "dead Cmd+Z in slides text boxes / demo app" symptom it prevents. The claim that "nothing covers the Mem path" is also wrong: memory.test.ts:317-337 drives snapshot() -> batch() on a real MemDocStore and asserts canUndo() === false after one undo, with boundary cases at :339 (empty batch) and :347 (write between snapshot and batch is not adopted). The slides path uses this same class (text-box-editor.ts:33 imports MemDocStore from ../store/memory.js, instantiates at :431, wires saveSnapshot at :680 and undo at :681-687), and withUndoUnit() is just `this.doc.batch(fn)` (text-editor.ts:3839-3842), so no variant escapes the adoption logic. Code not present as described.
